translations.3:
This manual not only comprehensively and systematically introduces commonly used standards, formulas, and data for hydraulic cylinder design, but also provides technical requirements for hydraulic cylinders and cylinder components, design and manufacturing taboos for hydraulic cylinders, test methods for hydraulic cylinders, and numerous hydraulic cylinder product drawings verified through actual machine testing (or empirical testing), based on relevant standards and the author's practical experience in designing and manufacturing hydraulic machinery. Furthermore, through research and engineering experiments (including partial verification and re-inspection), it has selected hydraulic cylinder design and (re)manufacturing new technologies with practical value or engineering application prospects.

This manual features novel content, large information volume, extensive source materials, complete specifications, strong practicality, reliable data, and convenient use.

This manual is suitable for use by personnel engaged in selection, design, process planning, processing, assembly, testing, acceptance, on-site maintenance and upkeep, remanufacturing, and product marketing of hydraulic cylinders and hydraulic machinery, equipment, or devices. It can also serve as a reference for teachers and students in relevant specialties at institutions of higher learning.

Preface

In a hydraulic transmission system, power is transmitted and controlled through pressurized fluid in a closed circuit. The hydraulic cylinder is one of the components (parts) in such systems. It is a device that converts hydraulic power into linear mechanical force and motion. A hydraulic cylinder consists of moving parts and components (subcomponents), namely piston rods operating within the cylinder barrel, or piston rods and pistons that are coaxially integrated and move together.

In hydraulic transmission systems and components, besides oil tanks and piping, the most common technical design that engineers encounter is the hydraulic cylinder. Although hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing is relatively simple and straightforward compared to other hydraulic components or devices, truly designing and manufacturing a good hydraulic cylinder is quite difficult. This is because its operating conditions are more difficult to determine than those of hydraulic valves or pumps, and may be affected by unexpected factors. Furthermore, hydraulic cylinders are often produced in single units or small batches, making it difficult to achieve perfection in materials, heat treatment processes, process equipment, assembly, and inspection. Any small mistake can lead to serious accidents. Taking hydraulic press cylinders as an example, if the seal system is not properly designed, or if the dimensions, geometric tolerances, or surface roughness of designed, machined, and manufactured parts are not properly handled, internal and external leakage will occur. Even just replacing sealing rings can cause significant waste of labor and materials. Field incidents have occurred where heat treatment problems caused defects...
